info.name: Cassini Live
info.summary: Private live captions for Nextcloud Talk, with a choice of speech engines.
info.description:
Follow a Talk call in real time with live captions, in a transcript panel beside the call. Audio and captions stay on your infrastructure: no account, API key, GPU, recording or saved transcript.
## What you get
- **Live captions with names.** Each speaker's words appear under their Talk name, including your own. - **A transcript panel in the call sidebar.** Scroll back through the call; people who join late see what was said before they arrived. - **Seven languages on a CPU.** Whistle, bundled, recognises English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Polish, with automatic language detection. - **More accurate engines on request.** Administrators can switch the server to Nemotron English (NVIDIA Open Model License) or Nemotron Multilingual (OpenMDW-1.1). Their models are downloaded from dist.gocassini.com when chosen, not shipped in the image. - **Safe under load.** Cassini Live needs enforced CPU, memory and process limits, and captions fewer speakers rather than everyone late when the server can't keep up.
## Before you install: Talk's caption button
Talk currently sends its **Show captions** button only to an app with the id `live_transcription`, Nextcloud's own Live Transcription app. Cassini Live from the App Store has its own id, so Talk's button does not drive it. People turn captions on from Cassini Live's transcript panel instead, which they add to Talk once with a bookmarklet from `/index.php/apps/app_api/proxy/cassini_live/panel/`. Cassini Live and Nextcloud's Live Transcription can be installed together; Talk's button keeps driving Nextcloud's app.
## Requirements
- Nextcloud 33 to 35 with Talk's High-performance backend, AppAPI and a deploy daemon. - The HPB internal secret, entered once after installation on Cassini Live's settings page (Administration settings > Assistant, then ? next to Cassini Live). Its URL is discovered from Talk. - Linux with cgroup v2, and CPU, memory and PID limits on the container. Whistle needs about 2 GiB of container memory; Nemotron 2.25-3 GiB, and twice that on the host.
## Support
Questions and bugs: [GitHub issues](https://github.com/codemyriad/cassini-live/issues). Cassini Live is a companion to [Cassini](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/gocassini), which records and transcribes Talk meetings.

variable.name: CASSINI_TALK_SIGNALING_INTERNAL_SECRET
variable.description: The signalling server's [clients] internalsecret, not the shared secret in Talk settings. On AIO: docker exec nextcloud-aio-talk printenv INTERNAL_SECRET. Alternatively, leave this empty and enter it on the Cassini Live settings page after installation.

variable.name: CASSINI_TALK_HPB_URL
variable.description: Leave empty to discover from Talk. Override only when the container needs a different address. Can also be set on the Cassini Live settings page.

variable.name: CASSINI_LIVE_DEBUG_VIDEO
variable.description: Set to 1 to show aggregate server metrics as a video participant in the first captioned room. Visible to everyone there. One feed per server, 1 fps; stops under resource pressure. Default off. The admin-only diagnostics page shows the same without this option.
